content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Deployment Pipelines helps operate an application safely outside the developer’s machine. Production readiness requires observable behavior, controlled failure, recovery evidence and safe configuration.

content_blocks.title: What to learn
content_blocks.text: This lesson covers: Automated tests before release; Build and deployment stages; Environment separation; Rollback procedures. Keep the source terms intact; for each one, name the component that owns the behavior, the inputs/assumptions, and the expected result.

items.title: Automated tests before release
items.text: For automated tests before release, identify the component responsible, the input it receives, and the observable result it should produce.

items.title: Build and deployment stages
items.text: Verify this setting on a clean runtime rather than assuming local development behavior transfers to production.

items.title: Environment separation
items.text: When applying environment separation, keep the implementation small, document version-dependent behavior, and verify it with a focused check.

items.title: Rollback procedures
items.text: Connect rollback procedures to deployment and production operations by tracing one example from its input through the observable output.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Deployment Pipelines
content_blocks.code:
# Development only: flask --app app run --debug
# Production example for a package with a create_app() factory:
# gunicorn "myproject:create_app()" --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT --workers 2
# Store SECRET_KEY and DATABASE_URL in the hosting platform's environment.
# Do not enable the interactive debugger in production.
content_blocks.expected_output: Use the framework development server locally only. In production, the host should run a supported production WSGI server with reviewed environment settings.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Verify the hosting platform’s startup command, port binding, secrets, database connectivity, TLS/proxy trust, migrations, health check and rollback plan.

content_blocks.title: Before using this beyond practice
content_blocks.text: Validate untrusted input at the server boundary, keep secrets out of source code, and test the failure path. Optional extensions or hosting infrastructure are separate dependencies unless stated otherwise.

content.expected_result: Use the framework development server locally only. In production, the host should run a supported production WSGI server with reviewed environment settings.
content.run_instructions: Verify the hosting platform’s startup command, port binding, secrets, database connectivity, TLS/proxy trust, migrations, health check and rollback plan.
troubleshooting: Confirm the expected virtual environment and installed dependency versions before diagnosing framework behavior.
Check route/method, input shape, status code, traceback location and relevant configuration one at a time.
For database or third-party integration examples, use isolated local resources and explicit timeouts; do not use production credentials.
content.reset_steps: Stop the local development server, reset only disposable local practice data if needed, and remove temporary artifacts created by the exercise. Never delete production data or migration history to reset practice.
content.try_it_yourself: Apply deployment pipelines to a tiny local Flask app. Predict what a normal request should do, test one invalid or boundary case, and record expected versus observed behavior.
progressive_hints: Name the Flask component or ecosystem tool responsible for deployment pipelines.
Run the smallest example in an isolated local project and compare the actual response with the stated expected result.
Add one negative or boundary test, then check the linked version-specific official documentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a fragment without checking its imports, app configuration or dependencies.
common_mistakes.why: Many Flask examples assume a configured app and a specific runtime or extension version.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the run instructions, record the Flask/Python version and test the smallest behavior first.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the successful request path.
common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, unsupported methods, unauthorized objects and service failures often have different behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a negative or boundary test and assert the status code and response contract.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a local example as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Secret management, concurrency, deployment, monitoring and failure recovery need separate design decisions.
common_mistakes.fix: Review the matching deployment and security references before publication or real use.

content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: trace one input through the relevant framework component, keep validation and authorization explicit, and write the smallest test that demonstrates the intended behavior. This note does not claim the example was executed.
